## Trial `wireguard-gateway-rhel7__SwG6GVS`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** The executor built a functioning topology matching the task contract: node2 serves an app on 8080 over a private node1/node2 LAN that node3 has no structural path into; a WireGuard tunnel was terminated on node1 (native VyOS) with a userspace client built from source on node3 (whose 3.10 kernel lacks native WireGuard support); and firewall scoping on node2 was verified, both before and after a full reboot of all three nodes, to permit app access from node3 only through the tunnel while directly refusing access over the default network. The independent node-restart evidence protocol was completed and cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle snapshots for all three nodes, with healthy pre-restart state, acknowledged restarts, distinct post-restart boot identities, and full recovery of app/tunnel/route state. Hygiene is only mildly impacted by an unnecessary, low-risk elrepo-release package left installed on node2, which never needed WireGuard tooling.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.800 | 0.900 | 96/9 (+14 dropped) |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **R1 — Satisfied:** node2 serves an application on TCP port 8080
  - **Why:** python2 SimpleHTTPServer is bound to 0.0.0.0:8080 on node2, wrapped in a systemd webapp.service (enabled, active), and serves content confirmed via curl both locally and remotely. The after-executor listening-sockets snapshot independently confirms *:8080 held by python2.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-deb09b0ba4434a68`, `cmd-5116f80d7e7e4d39`, `cmd-ab0b549b00ff46b2`, `global:after_executor:node2:listening-sockets`
- **R2 — Satisfied:** node1 and node2 share a private network that node3 is structurally outside of
  - **Why:** node1 eth1 (10.50.50.1/24, VyOS committed/saved) and node2 eth1 (10.50.50.2/24) form a private LAN with confirmed bidirectional reachability (ping and curl). node3 was confirmed to have only eth0 on the shared default network with no second NIC, structurally excluding it from the private LAN.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-a263d1f1009b46af`, `cmd-956326c367d0482d`, `cmd-e330ed62cd3a47a2`, `cmd-37df144398c7452e`, `cmd-bc598041cc4c47f1`, `cmd-77a956d038f147e2`
- **R3 — Satisfied:** A WireGuard tunnel terminated on node1 exists and is functional
  - **Why:** Native VyOS wg0 interface on node1 was configured with generated keys, a peer entry for node3, committed and saved, and shown up with correct address. A live handshake with node3 was directly observed both before and after node1's restart.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-4988d226ca434890`, `cmd-2281bdccd08a42ad`, `cmd-29bab5be48b2462c`, `cmd-224b4fa72db242d4`, `cmd-8c1328ee34214b0e`
- **R4 — Satisfied:** node3 can reach node2's app on 8080 only via the WireGuard tunnel through node1, not directly
  - **Why:** Because node3's kernel (3.10) lacks native WireGuard, wireguard-tools and wireguard-go were built from source and a persistent wg-quick@wg0 tunnel established to node1 with a successful, re-established handshake. A static route on node2 sent tunnel-destined return traffic via node1. After node2's firewall was scoped to expose 8080 only on the eth1 (private) zone, node3 direct access to node2's public/default-network IP was confirmed refused (EXIT=7 curl error) while access via the tunnel path to node2's private IP succeeded, both before and after all three nodes were restarted.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-a9bfe48c459a485e`, `cmd-72adc360d73444db`, `cmd-88dfe5b7f7df4a66`, `cmd-2feca923ad4645e6`, `cmd-0168da1a63eb453e`, `cmd-cb7d372491fb4fbb`, `cmd-6c3f6198da294337`, `cmd-72d98a7986d146a8`, `cmd-5fa0e9afd090433b`, `cmd-98008adfa6574d36`
- **R5 — Satisfied:** Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on every managed node (independent of task contract)
  - **Why:** All three nodes show a complete restart cycle: pre-restart healthy baseline and boot_id, an acknowledged restart command, a distinct post-restart boot_id, and recovered application/tunnel/network state. node1: ebd78841...→60449fa0..., eth1/wg0/peer config intact post-reboot. node2: 738d0aac...→a919a07f..., webapp.service active and route/eth1 intact (after a pre-reboot corrective restart of a failed webapp unit). node3: 3dba43a5...→915d5f4c..., wg-quick@wg0 active with automatic re-handshake. All boot-id transitions are independently corroborated by the fixed before/after-executor lifecycle snapshots, and full end-to-end app reachability through the tunnel was re-verified after all three restarts completed.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-224b4fa72db242d4`, `cmd-ba3c9e5e8ddb4ed0`, `cmd-1284af0712aa4f84`, `cmd-8c1328ee34214b0e`, `cmd-a7c61595213b4a77`, `cmd-c4e2b0c49bdf4c6b`, `cmd-c77a08c3bb7a4cbc`, `cmd-002d4e0285c34f93`, `cmd-4a3e2e4c61894c73`, `cmd-98f3ce4cd3af4555`, `cmd-2ed65e8bb26f4e8b`, `cmd-ba4c187ade8d47c5`, `cmd-5fa0e9afd090433b`, `cmd-98008adfa6574d36`, `global:before_prepare:node1:boot-identity`, `global:after_executor:node1:boot-identity`, `global:before_prepare:node2:boot-identity`, `global:after_executor:node2:boot-identity`, `global:before_prepare:node3:boot-identity`, `global:after_executor:node3:boot-identity`

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.800**. Most state-changing commands map clearly to prerequisite installation (gcc/make/libmnl-devel for building wireguard-tools/wireguard-go on node3), the private LAN/app/firewall setup, or bounded diagnostic/corrective actions (e.g. restarting a failed webapp.service before establishing the reboot baseline, or the public-zone 8080 opening on node2 that was later removed once the eth1-only wgnet zone was created). One unnecessary and unreverted mutation stands out: elrepo-release was installed via rpm on node2 (cmd-a61e5c4384dd475f) and a subsequent kmod-wireguard/wireguard-tools install was attempted there (cmd-c8c20c6739604cb1), even though node2 never functions as a WireGuard endpoint in the final design (only node1 and node3 need WireGuard tooling). The yum install failed (package unavailable) so no wireguard package was pulled in, but the elrepo-release repo definition itself was left installed on node2 with no functional role — low-risk, non-destructive residue. Additional failed epel-release/elrepo attempts on both node2 and node3 did not mutate state (transactions failed) and are treated as discovery.

Hygiene evidence: `cmd-a61e5c4384dd475f`, `cmd-c8c20c6739604cb1`, `cmd-1f9ac14545ba473f`, `cmd-cce6935151c345b5`, `cmd-691939f9cec947f8`, `cmd-0168da1a63eb453e`, `cmd-76955918628c408b`

### Comments and limitations

- The executor's final report cited several evidence-item command IDs (cmd-6c18adac85384f01, cmd-6c7ea9c0ed4001, cmd-6c7ea9c0ed4002, cmd-6c9c8ac0ed4001, cmd-6c9c8ac0ed4002) that do not correspond to any command in the captured timeline; the underlying claim is still supported by other, valid command IDs in the same evidence group.
- Native package-manager consistency checks (package-health) were unavailable (timed out) on node2 and node3 at every lifecycle snapshot, so package-state integrity beyond the specific commands observed cannot be independently confirmed for those nodes.
- The full end-to-end path check immediately after all three restarts initially timed out (cmd-5fa0e9afd090433b) and only succeeded after an additional ~20s wait (cmd-98008adfa6574d36) for the WireGuard persistent-keepalive handshake to re-establish; this is consistent with expected tunnel re-convergence behavior rather than a failure, but it is a bounded transient worth noting.
- Executor evidence item 6 referenced unknown command IDs: cmd-6c18adac85384f01, cmd-6c7ea9c0ed4001, cmd-6c7ea9c0ed4002, cmd-6c9c8ac0ed4001, cmd-6c9c8ac0ed4002
- Operational hygiene was below a full pass (0.800); review the hygiene explanation above separately from functional success.
- Verifier confidence was 0.900; this is evidence confidence for this trial, not a repeatability estimate.
